title: Security/privacy review for perf-canary (prompts, logs/metrics retention, access controls)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal: complete a security/privacy review for the production perf-regression canary.

Scope:
1) Prompts / payloads: ensure the canary prompt set contains no customer data or anything that could be mistaken for customer content.
2) Logging + metrics: confirm we are not emitting prompt text or other sensitive payloads into logs/traces/metrics; validate retention aligns with Redwood standards.
3) Access controls: confirm least-privilege access to the perf-canary dashboards and metrics namespaces, and that oncall automation (incident-bot) posts only safe context.

Why this matters:
- Canary traffic is synthetic but runs in prod regions and shares observability pipelines. Any accidental inclusion of real data (or overly verbose logging) would create an unnecessary privacy and compliance risk.
- Canary is designed to be always-on, so mistakes can accumulate quickly (high-frequency signals + long retention).

Acceptance criteria:
- Prompt set is audited and documented as synthetic/public-domain/self-authored with no customer identifiers.
- Canary runner + runtime instrumentation confirm no prompt text, request bodies, or tool arguments are logged at INFO by default.
- Metrics/traces contain only approved labels (model, region, gpu_sku, runtime_build, scheduler_mode, canary_source) and do not include user-provided fields.
- Retention and access controls documented (who can view what; how to request access).
- Security/Compliance sign-off recorded here along with any follow-up hardening tasks.

Proposed decisions (to validate in review):
- Prompt material:
  - Only synthetic prompts authored by Redwood, or excerpts from permissively licensed public datasets.
  - Prompts stored in repo as static fixtures; each prompt has a stable ID (prompt_id) and category (shape) but text is not emitted to logs/metrics.
  - Prompts must not include emails, phone numbers, addresses, API keys, customer names, or anything that looks like real account data.
- Logging:
  - Canary runner logs request metadata only (model, region, streaming_mode, token counts, prompt_id) and never logs raw prompt text.
  - Runtime request tracing: allow span tags for runtime_build, kernel_id, scheduler_mode, gpu_sku, batch stats; explicitly disallow request body capture.
  - incident-bot payload: include links + version diffs + slice breakdowns, but no prompt text.
- Retention:
  - Metrics: follow standard metrics retention (13 months in aggregated form); high-cardinality raw series are downsampled; no per-request payloads.
  - Logs: 14 days for runner logs; 7 days for debug logs (if enabled temporarily); canary-specific debug dumps gated and default-off.
  - Traces: 7 days, sampled; canary spans are tagged source=perf-canary for filtering.
- Access:
  - Grafana folder + metric namespaces restricted to Eng (SRE/Runtime/Telemetry) and oncall; access via INT-3321 flow.

Links:
- Initiative: ENG-2841
- Workload matrix: (Drive) shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/perf-canary-workload-matrix-sheet
- Metrics spec draft: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/perf-canary-metric-spec.json
- Alert tuning notes: shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/perf-canary-alert-tuning-notes

Follow-ups (if gaps found):
- Add pre-commit / CI check to prevent prompt fixtures containing common PII patterns.
- Add lint rule to prevent logging request bodies for source=perf-canary.
- Ensure debug export endpoints are canary-gated + access-controlled.
comments: 2026-01-22 — Talia Benson: Spinning up a dedicated ticket for the privacy/security pass before phase-1 rollout. Please treat as a blocker for enabling in us-east beyond the initial smoke test. Owners: Paula (policy), Logan (telemetry), Rafael (oncall automation), Omar (runtime instrumentation).

2026-01-24 — Logan Wright: Telemetry side: metric schema is safe as long as we don’t add prompt_id as a high-cardinality label. OK to keep prompt_id in runner logs (short retention) and as a trace attribute only if it’s low-cardinality and not searchable outside the restricted trace project. Prefer prompt_shape + workload_scenario over prompt_id in metrics.

2026-01-27 — Omar El-Sayed: Runtime tags for canary are request-scoped; confirmed we do not emit request bodies anywhere in the runtime metrics path. Kernel-selection debug export is gated behind source=perf-canary and writes only kernel_id + fallback_reason + runtime_build (no payload).

2026-01-30 — Rafael Mendes: incident-bot formatting updated so the Slack post includes: model, region, gpu_sku, runtime_build (current vs baseline), scheduler_mode, last deploy annotation, and dashboard/runbook links. No prompt details included. Also ensured the webhook payload does not contain raw trace/log excerpts by default (links only).

2026-02-03 — Paula Mendes: Prompt set review complete. All prompts are synthetic and stored under perf-canary repo fixtures; removed two prompts that contained what looked like a real company name (even though public) to avoid confusion. Added a short README documenting prompt provenance + a checklist for additions (no identifiers, no secrets, no customer-like strings).

2026-02-06 — Talia Benson: Marking done. Security/Compliance reviewed the approach asynchronously and confirmed: (1) synthetic prompts only, (2) no prompt text in logs/metrics/traces, (3) retention/access consistent with internal standards. Action items captured as follow-up tasks in ENG-2889 (PII lint for prompt fixtures) and ENG-2890 (log guardrails for canary runner).
